facts.statement: A nearly complete hadrosaurid skeleton was discovered in 1961 at the Syuk-Syuk locality in southern Kazakhstan, 45 km north of Tashkent.
facts.quote: In 1961, a nearly complete skeleton of a hadrosaurid was found at the Syuk-Syuk locality of the Dabrazinskaya Svita of southern Kazakhstan, 45 km north of Tashkent, Uzbekistan.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen PIN 2230 is an almost complete skeleton missing only the snout, hands, left foot, and tail tip, making it the most complete dinosaur known from the former Soviet Union.
facts.quote: The specimen, PIN No. 2230, was an almost complete skeleton only missing the snout of the skull, the hands and left foot, and the end of the tail, being the most complete dinosaur known not only from Kazakhstan but also from the entire Soviet Union.

facts.statement: Soviet paleontologist Anatoly Konstantinovich Rozhdestvensky described the species as Procheneosaurus convincens in 1968.
facts.quote: PIN 2230 was described in 1968 by Soviet palaeontologist Anatoly Konstantinovich Rozhdestvensky as the new species Procheneosaurus convincens

facts.statement: Canadian paleontologists Phil R. Bell and Kirstin S. Brink revisited and partly redescribed the taxon in 2013, focusing on the skull.
facts.quote: "Procheneosaurus" convincens was revisited and partly redescribed in 2013 by Canadian palaeontologists Phil R. Bell and Kirstin S. Brink, who focused their study on the skull due to its diagnostic ability.

facts.statement: Kazaklambia convincens lived in Asia during the Late Cretaceous Santonian stage, approximately between 86.3 and 83.6 million years ago.
facts.quote: Kazaklambia convincens es la única especie conocida del género extinto Kazaklambia de dinosaurio hadrosáurido lambeosaurino que vivió a finales del período el Cretácico, hace aproximadamente entre 86,3 y 83,6 durante el Santoniense, en lo que es hoy Asia.

facts.statement: Kazaklambia is morphologically distinct from other Eurasian taxa and juveniles of similar age due to a thickened dome on the postorbital bone, doming of the nasal bone, and a frontal length-to-width ratio of less than one.
facts.quote: Bell & Brink suggested that Kazaklambia is morphologically distinct from other Eurasian taxa and known juvenile lambeosaurines at a similar ontogenetic stage in having a prefrontal process of the postorbital with a thickened dome lateral to the frontal dome, doming of the nasal above and in front of the orbit, and a frontal length/width ratio of less than one.

facts.statement: Bell and Brink assigned Kazaklambia to the Lambeosaurinae subfamily in a basal position in 2013.
facts.quote: Bell and Brink (2013) assigned Kazaklambia to the Lambeosaurinae, in a basal position.

facts.statement: A 2021 phylogenetic analysis identified Kazaklambia as a primitive member of the Lambeosaurini tribe, though broader relationships within Lambeosaurinae remain unresolved.
facts.quote: The phylogenetic analysis of Ramírez-Velasco and colleagues in 2021 found Kazaklambia to be a primitive member of Lambeosaurini, though much of the relationships of Lambeosaurinae could not be resolved.

facts.statement: American paleontologist Peter Dodson rejected Procheneosaurus as a distinct genus in 1975, creating uncertainty about the validity of P. convincens.
facts.quote: The status of Procheneosaurus as a distinct genus was rejected by American palaeontologist Peter Dodson in 1975 in a study that found the North American species of the genus were actually juveniles of Corythosaurus and Lambeosaurus, leading to uncertainty regarding the status of P. convincens.

facts.statement: There is a debate regarding the species' validity, with some researchers considering it a synonym of Jaxartosaurus while others support its separation based on skull anatomy.
facts.quote: American palaeontologists David B. Weishampel and John R. Horner in 1990 and 2004, who considered Procheneosaurus convincens as a junior synonym of Jaxartosaurus, but was supported by British palaeontologist David B. Norman and American palaeontologist Hans-Dieter Sues in 2000.

facts.statement: The species name 'convincens' refers to the specimen being the most complete dinosaur ever found in the Soviet Union at the time, proving dinosaurs existed in that geological horizon.
facts.quote: El nombre de especie se refiere al hecho de que el espécimen, el dinosaurio más completo jamás descubierto en el entonces territorio soviético, probaba de forma convincente que los dinosaurios podían ser hallados sobre el así llamado "horizonte de dinosaurios".

facts.statement: Kazaklambia is known from the juvenile holotype specimen PIN 2230, which lacks the snout, lower jaw front, some dorsal vertebrae, and the tail tip.
facts.quote: Kazaklambia es conocido a partir del esqueleto de un individuo juvenil, el holotipo PIN 2230, hallado por G.A. Belenkiy en 1961, que solo carece del hocico, el frente de la mandíbula inferior, algunas vértebras dorsales y el final de la cola.

rejected.statement: In 2013, Bell and Brink established the new genus name Kazaklambia because the juvenile specimen could be distinguished from other similar lambeosaurines, honoring the country of discovery.
rejected.quote: Bell and Brink found that despite its juvenile status, "P." convincens could be distinguished from all other juvenile lambeosaurines as well as Aralosaurus and Jaxartosaurus of similar age and location, so they gave it the new genus name Kazaklambia in reference to the country of discovery and its status as a member of Lambeosaurinae.

rejected.statement: Kazaklambia is an extinct herbivorous lambeosaurine dinosaur known from the Late Cretaceous Santonian stage of southern Kazakhstan.
rejected.quote: Kazaklambia is an extinct genus of herbivorous lambeosaurine dinosaur known from the Late Cretaceous Dabrazinskaya Svita (Santonian stage) of southern Kazakhstan.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'herbivorous lambeosaurine dinosaur known from the Late Cretaceous'
